overview: A single-service REST API for managing todo items, implemented in Go with net/http on port 9090. The service exposes list, create, and delete endpoints over HTTP with JSON payloads, uses file-based persistence for durability across restarts, and applies a mutex for safe concurrent access.
requirements: Provide GET /todos endpoint returning all todos ordered by creation time, 200 with empty array when none exist
Provide POST /todos endpoint accepting JSON {title}, validating non-empty title with max 255 chars, returning 201 with generated id and createdAt
Provide DELETE /todos/{id} endpoint returning 204 on success and 404 if not found
Each todo has id (UUID), title, completed (bool, default false), createdAt (RFC3339)
Return 400 for validation errors and malformed JSON, 404 for missing resources, 500 for server errors, all with consistent {error, code} JSON shape
Persist todos across restarts via file-based storage
Ensure concurrency safety with mutex-protected access and unique IDs

components.name: todo-api
components.openAPISpec:
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Todo API
  version: 1.0.0
servers:
  - url: http://localhost:9090
paths:
  /health:
    get:
      summary: Health check
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: object
                properties:
                  status: {type: string}
  /todos:
    get:
      summary: List todos
      responses:
        '200':
          description: List of todos
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Todo'}
    post:
      summary: Create todo
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/CreateTodoRequest'}
      responses:
        '201':
          description: Created
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Todo'}
        '400':
          description: Validation error
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'}
  /todos/{id}:
    delete:
      summary: Delete todo
      parameters:
        - name: id
          in: path
          required: true
          schema: {type: string}
      responses:
        '204': {description: Deleted}
        '404':
          description: Not found
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Error'}
components:
  schemas:
    Todo:
      type: object
      properties:
        id: {type: string}
        title: {type: string}
        completed: {type: boolean}
        createdAt: {type: string, format: date-time}
    CreateTodoRequest:
      type: object
      required: [title]
      properties:
        title: {type: string, maxLength: 255}
        completed: {type: boolean}
    Error:
      type: object
      properties:
        error: {type: string}
        code: {type: string}
components.componentAgentInstructions: Build a Go service using net/http on port 9090. Endpoints: GET /health -> {status:"ok"}; GET /todos -> JSON array sorted by createdAt ascending (empty array if none); POST /todos -> accept JSON {title, completed?}, validate title non-empty and <=255 chars, generate UUID id, set createdAt=time.Now().UTC().Format(RFC3339), default completed=false, return 201 with created todo; DELETE /todos/{id} -> 204 if deleted, 404 with {error,code} if not found. Error response shape: {"error":"msg","code":"CODE"}. Use codes VALIDATION_ERROR (400), INVALID_JSON (400), NOT_FOUND (404), INTERNAL_ERROR (500). Content-Type application/json for all responses. Use sync.RWMutex protecting an in-memory map plus persist to a JSON file (path from env TODO_DATA_FILE, default /data/todos.json) on every write; load on startup (create empty if missing). Use google/uuid for ids. Log each request (method, path, status, duration) and errors via log package. Recover from panics in middleware returning 500 INTERNAL_ERROR without leaking details. Dockerfile: multi-stage build, final image runs binary, EXPOSE 9090, create /data dir.
